significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a "compact (k<=10), query-conditioned set of attention heads" causally routes internally recoverable facts to the output, with expression across query phrasings predictively coupled to gate activation; this is a form-(iii) relation combined with a form-(ii) causal storage-versus-routing decomposition. It would establish both a phenomenon—fixed facts become expressible or hidden as the query-to-gate mapping changes—and a mechanism, fixing expectations that gate activity rather than MLP content should track those changes and that gate intervention should restore expression selectively. Geva et al., "Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models" (2023), separates MLP-mediated subject enrichment from attention-mediated attribute extraction, while Hase et al., "Does Localization Inform Editing?" (2023), shows that localization and editability can diverge, so settling whether an attention router explains that divide would materially constrain live mechanistic explanations; a negative result would rule out the compact attention-dominant account, although the claim's fallback to a "distributed gate" prevents it from ruling out gating altogether. Verified true and false are distinguishable for the compact causal claim, and the topic-substitution check passes: deleting the compact router, query-conditioned coupling, and storage/routing decomposition leaves only the broad assigned topic, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two concrete handles: "gate-head features" that predict expression and the interventions "amplifying gate-head attention to the subject token or patching gate-head outputs," giving auditors a diagnostic and practitioners a reversible control. The predictor is ex ante at the answer level because it flags likely expression failure from the query-conditioned forward pass before the answer is emitted, while the intervention can then act during that window; identifying the original hidden-knowledge cases is otherwise post hoc. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion predicts a transferable relation—higher activation of a compact router should predict expression and manipulating it should recover latent facts—rather than merely prescribing a search procedure, although exact heads and numerical performance would still need recalibration and the asserted scope is principally factual QA across GPT-J, Llama, and Qwen-class 6–8B models. Downstream users include "knowledge-editing practitioners" and "reliability auditors," and the topic-substitution check passes because the usable predictor and decode-time routing intervention disappear when the claim-specific mechanism is removed.
